title: The New Epicenter of Global Terror
gist: Teaser (paywalled after intro) by Eghosa E. Osaghae arguing Africa, with weak states and rare earths, is the new epicenter of transnational extremism, even as the US and Europe have turned their attention to China, Ukraine and the Middle East.

themes.theme: Africa as the new terror epicenter

insights.claim: Eghosa E. Osaghae argues that Africa's weak states and rare earths are driving transnational extremism, making the continent the new epicenter of global terror.
insights.speaker: Eghosa E. Osaghae
insights.so_what: Rising security risk around African critical-mineral supply chains; factor into rare-earth sourcing and mining-jurisdiction risk.
insights.quote: How Africa’s Weak States and Rare Earths Drive Transnational Extremism

insights.claim: Since the defeat of the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria and the 2021 US withdrawal from Afghanistan, Washington and many European allies have shifted focus to confrontation with China and the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East rather than transnational extremism.
insights.speaker: Eghosa E. Osaghae
insights.so_what: Western attention deficit implies less counterterror support for African states and higher risk of escalation in mining regions.
insights.quote: more preoccupied with the growing confrontation with China, and with the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East

insights.claim: The Western de-prioritization of counterterrorism has been buttressed by a general decline in terrorist attacks in many parts of the world since ISIS's peak.
insights.speaker: Eghosa E. Osaghae
insights.so_what: Global aggregate decline can mask regional concentration — the author implies Africa is the exception.
insights.quote: a general decline in terrorist attacks in many parts of the world since ISIS’s peak

insights.claim: Islamic State-linked militants carried out an attack in Cantine-Aloya, Democratic Republic of the Congo, in November 2026.
insights.speaker: Eghosa E. Osaghae
insights.so_what: Ongoing IS-linked violence in eastern DRC, a key critical-minerals region.
insights.quote: Islamic State-linked militants, Cantine-Aloya, Democratic Republic of the Congo, November 2026
